group: LSV Asset Management — top 50 holdings by position value (Q1'26 13F)
takeaway: Of the 49 screened names (one position, DOX, wasn't returned by the data provider), 13 introduced a genuinely new LTIP metric in their latest grant cycle — the rest either left their metric set unchanged or only relabeled existing metrics. The clearest signal is a tilt toward balance-sheet and cash discipline: AIG added tangible book value per share, MPC added relative FCF-per-share, FDX added ROIC, and CVS added a debt-paydown ratio. A second cluster is pharma reweighting toward EPS (PFE, GILD). Several apparent 'changes' were filtered out as pure relabels (MRK, BAC, MTG, QCOM, PHM), which is where most naive screens would produce false positives.
classification_rule: A metric is 'new' if its normalized base name (tranche-year suffixes stripped, rTSR-modifiers and gates excluded, common abbreviations canonicalized) is present in the latest metric-bearing LTIP cycle but absent from the prior one. Pure relabels (e.g. 'Non-GAAP EPS' vs 'Non-GAAP Earnings Per Share (EPS)') and 'Relative X' prefix changes were reviewed by hand and excluded as not-new.
footer: Source: Verity (InsiderScore) long-term incentive plan data, Form DEF 14A. Describes incentive-plan design, not company quality or stock merit — not investment advice.

points.note: CEO transition reshaped the plan into discrete product-revenue, pipeline and BD goals; heaviest redesign in the book.

new: Adjusted Tangible Book Value per Share
points.note: Adds a book-value-per-share target and a calendar-year combined-ratio measure — a tilt toward capital and underwriting quality.
Swaps three strategic sub-metrics for a debt-paydown ratio, a Stars measure and a customer-engagement goal — deleveraging now explicitly paid for.
Drops the EV-product 'eProducts' metrics for relative revenue growth and cumulative EPS — a step back from the EV-transition scorecard toward conventional financials.

new: Relative Change in FCF per Share
points.note: Long a 100%-rTSR plan; now layers in a relative FCF-per-share metric — first cash-return financial measure in the LTIP.

new: Relative Operating Cash Flow % of Revenue
points.note: Reframes cash-flow and margin goals as peer-relative — management now judged against other OEMs on cash and margin, not just absolute targets.
Replaces a capex-intensity metric with ROIC — capital-efficiency framed as a return rather than a spend ratio.
Adds an EPS metric and drops the very-long-dated 7-year TSR — a shift toward a more conventional, nearer-term earnings measure.
Replaces the long-standing net-product-revenue target with EPS growth — first earnings-based metric in the LTIP, a profitability tilt.
Broadens the growth metric from fee revenue to total revenue — net interest income now counts toward the long-term payout.
Reframes the two financial goals from three-year CAGRs to annual growth and adds a margin-growth dimension — a profitability emphasis on top of growth.
Swaps the operating-margin metric for an operating-income (dollar) metric — a subtle shift from rate to absolute profit.
Reverts to a 100%-relative-TSR plan after a one-cycle experiment with revenue-based PSUs; a reversion rather than a fresh metric, flagged for context.
